title: Bollywood Splits Over NEET Protests as Neha Bhasin Slams Bhumi Pednekar's Remarks
excerpt: Singer Neha Bhasin's sharp rebuke of actress Bhumi Pednekar over protest language highlights a deepening rift in the film industry's response to India's student-led demonstrations.
body:
• Singer Neha Bhasin criticised actress Bhumi Pednekar for questioning the language used by NEET protesters, telling her 'gooda nahi hai toh chup rehna best hai behen' (if you don't have the guts, just stay quiet)
  • The spat reflects a growing divide in Bollywood between celebrities who fully back the protesters and those who have urged restraint over slogans and language
  • The NEET paper leak protests, which forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign, have drawn unprecedented celebrity involvement and public debate

The fault lines in Bollywood's response to India's NEET exam protests sharpened this week after singer Neha Bhasin publicly called out actress Bhumi Pednekar for focusing on the language used by demonstrators rather than the police action against them.

"Gooda nahi hai toh chup rehna best hai behen," Bhasin wrote on social media — roughly translated as "if you don't have the guts, just stay quiet, sister." The remark was directed at Pednekar's comments questioning the behaviour of student protesters, particularly the use of anti-government slogans during the Cockroach Janta Party-led demonstrations over the alleged NEET exam paper leak.

What Triggered the Backlash

Pednekar had initially expressed support for the student movement, writing on Instagram that "we owe it to the youth of our country to ensure this movement doesn't resort to violence" and calling for dialogue rather than confrontation. But her subsequent comments questioning the language and slogans used by some protesters drew sharp criticism from those who argued she was deflecting attention from police brutality.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2084813787727815116

Actress Dia Mirza weighed in on the same side as Bhasin, posting that the focus should be on "police brutality" rather than protest language. Pednekar's former acting teacher also publicly criticised her remarks, according to ThePrint. India Today reported that the internet had "roasted" the actress for her comments on anti-Modi slogans raised during the demonstrations.

The Bigger Picture: Bollywood and the NEET Crisis

The celebrity spat is a microcosm of a broader reckoning. The NEET paper leak scandal — which led to the cancellation of the exam taken by nearly 2 million students, a re-test in June, and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan — has prompted an unusually vocal response from Bollywood.

Actors including Diljit Dosanjh, Sonakshi Sinha, Huma Qureshi, Riteish Deshmukh and Sonam Bajwa rallied behind the student protesters after the July 20 march on Parliament was met with tear gas and baton charges. Veteran actors Shabana Azmi and Prakash Raj joined demonstrations in person. Naseeruddin Shah released an emotional video criticising both the police response and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's handling of the crisis.

"We stand in solidarity with the youth of our country. Their voices deserve to be heard — loud, clear, and without fear."

— Riteish Deshmukh, on X

The CBI has since filed charges against 13 people in connection with the leaked question papers, including three National Testing Agency subject experts and several middlemen. India's Supreme Court ordered that no coercive action be taken against protesters and directed the release of all under-18 detainees.

A Divided Film Industry

The Bhasin-Pednekar exchange illustrates a tension that has surfaced repeatedly in India's entertainment industry during politically charged moments: the line between supporting a cause and policing how ordinary people express their frustration. Bhasin's critique — that celebrities who lack the courage to fully back protesters should stay silent — resonated with those who saw Pednekar's comments as an attempt to appear sympathetic while distancing herself from the movement's sharper edges.

For the diaspora, the NEET protests have become one of the most watched stories out of India this year. Solidarity demonstrations have been held in New York, London, Berlin and other cities, with participants adopting the movement's "Main bhi cockroach" slogan. The Bollywood divide over how far to go in supporting the protests mirrors a broader conversation in the diaspora about solidarity, tone and political risk.
